new_sources.summary: Generation Z is leaving institutional Christianity at unprecedented rates, yet many young people retain genuine spiritual hunger. This article argues that Billie Eilish’s music functions as a contemporary iteration of the biblical lament tradition: a sacred whisper addressed to the mystery of suffering, in the same register the Church has largely abandoned. Drawing on Karen O’Donnell’s trauma theology, particularly her practice of hopelessness, and on a close reading of Eilish’s songs alongside the lament psalms, the article makes the constructive case that the psalms of lament and her music form a continuous human crying-out rather than two separate registers, one sacred and one secular.
